steps.notes: Rows-first (Nt,Ny,Nx) impl passes bit-exact; literal reading of prompt sentence 'second and third dimensions are x and y' gives (Nt,Nx,Ny) and FAILS all 3 tests (shape mismatch vs target (2,5,10)).
Straightforward; corner-skip rule explicit and pinned by targets (corners (0,0),(0,9),(4,0) left unchanged in targets). Only modifies the given time slice.
Passes ONLY with '+axis derivative' sign (T_b = T_inner - N on left/top, + N on right/bottom). Spec-literal outward-normal convention fails 0/3. Right/bottom branch never exercised with nonzero N.

Bit-exact with: per-point alpha_ij*laplacian (central diff, dx=dy=1), dt=1/(4 max(a1,a2)), BCs (Dirichlet then Neumann) applied to slice 0 AND to each new slice t+1 with Neumann reading post-update t+1 neighbors; corners never written (stay 0 for t>=1, confirmed in targets).

findings.evidence: Prompt: 'The boundary normal should point outward from each boundary.' Under that convention, left boundary (outward n = -x, forward difference) gives dT/dn = (T[i,0]-T[i,1])/dx = N -> T[i,0] = T[i,1] + N. The frozen targets encode the OPPOSITE on left/top: test 1 (bc=[[1,0,20]], left boundary) target grid[0,1,0]=80 with neighbor grid[0,1,1]=100, i.e. T_b = T_inner - N; test 2 (top row, N=40): target row0 = row1 - 40 (60 over material 1, 10 over material 2); test 3 (left col, N=100): target = 10-100 = -90. So targets encode dT/d(+axis) = N (the INWARD normal on left/top). Dynamic proof: review/work/45/step_45.3_outward.py (spec-literal outward normal) FAILS 0/3 tests; review/work/45/step_45.3.py (+axis derivative) passes 3/3. On right/bottom the two conventions coincide, so the defect hits exactly the boundaries the tests use.
findings.suggested_fix: Either fix the prompt to state the actual convention ('the boundary value is dT/dx (resp. dT/dy) along the positive axis direction, approximated by forward difference at i=0/j=0 and backward difference at i=Ny-1/j=Nx-1, with dx=dy=1'), deleting the outward-normal sentence; or regenerate targets with the outward-normal sign (T_b = T_inner + N on all boundaries).

findings.evidence: 45.4's tests reuse add_neumann_bc with nonzero N on top/left boundaries (test 1: N=10 top+left; test 2: N=-10 top/left, +10 right/bottom). A solver whose 45.3 implements the prompt's stated outward-normal convention also fails 45.4: review/work/45/step_45.4_outward.py fails tests 1-2 with max abs deviation 164.4 and 222.9 (test 3 passes only because it has no Neumann BCs). The 45.3 sign defect therefore double-penalizes: the same spec-following choice fails two scored steps.
findings.suggested_fix: Same fix as 45.3 (align prompt convention with targets, or regenerate both 45.3 and 45.4 targets under the outward-normal convention).

findings.evidence: Step prompt: 'the first dimension is time, and the second and third dimensions are x and y coordinates of the grid', with 'Nx: x-dimension (number of columns)' and 'Ny: y-dimension (number of rows)'. The literal reading is shape (Nt, Nx, Ny); the frozen target for init_grid(2,10,5,...) has temp_grid shape (2,5,10) and diff_grid (5,10), i.e. (Nt, Ny, Nx) rows-first. Dynamic proof: review/work/45/step_45.1_literal.py ((Nt,Nx,Ny)) FAILS; review/work/45/step_45.1.py ((Nt,Ny,Nx)) passes 3/3. Disambiguating signals exist (rows/columns wording, bc [i=row, j=col] usage in the main I/O and steps 2-4), but only by contradicting the explicit dimension-order sentence in this step's own prompt.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the prompt sentence to 'the second dimension is y (rows, size Ny) and the third dimension is x (columns, size Nx)' so it matches the target layout (Nt, Ny, Nx).

findings.evidence: The prompt never states whether the boundary conditions are also enforced on the INITIAL slice (t=0) before time stepping, yet the targets require it: review/work/45/step_45.4_noBC0.py (identical solver, BCs only applied to slices t>=1) fails all 3 tests with max relative deviation 0.26%/0.27%/0.48% at t=190 (well above np.allclose rtol=1e-5). Step 45.1 even says 'Populate only the first time step with the initial temperatures', which suggests slice 0 = pure initial condition. Enforcing BCs after setting the IC is the canonical PDE workflow, so the intended choice is guessable, but a competent solver treating slice 0 as the unmodified IC fails every test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the 45.4 prompt: 'Apply both boundary-condition functions to the initial time slice (t=0) before time stepping, and to each newly computed slice.'

findings.evidence: All three 45.3 tests place nonzero Neumann values only on the LEFT or TOP boundary (forward-difference branch); the right/bottom (backward-difference) branch is exercised only at excluded corners. A wrong implementation using T_b = T_inner - N on ALL four boundaries passes 45.3 officially (review/work/45/step_45.3_allminus.py: PASS 3/3) and is then failed at 45.4 test 2 (the only test with nonzero N on right/bottom). So 45.3 certifies an implementation that 45.4 punishes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 45.3 test with nonzero N on the right column or bottom row, e.g. add_neumann_bc(init_grid(2,10,5,2,100,1,50,2)[0], 0, [[i, 9, 20] for i in range(5)]).

findings.evidence: The grid has two materials with different diffusivities, but the discretization at the interface is not pinned beyond 'central difference'. Target encodes the non-conservative per-point form T_new = T + dt*alpha[i,j]*laplacian(T). The conservative form d/dt T = div(alpha grad T) with arithmetic-mean face diffusivities (physically preferable for discontinuous alpha) fails tests 2-3 (max abs deviation 13.4 and 3.6; test 1 passes because alpha1=alpha2). The simple form is the more literal reading of 'central difference' + per-point diff_grid, so most solvers infer it, but a physics-careful solver can plausibly choose the conservative form and fail.
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly in the 45.4 prompt: 'use the update T[t+1,i,j] = T[t,i,j] + dt * alpha[i,j] * (central-difference Laplacian of T[t]) with dx=dy=1' (i.e., the non-conservative per-point-diffusivity form).

findings.evidence: Documentation typos repeated in problem_io and the 45.1/45.4 docstrings: the parameter list shows 'T1: the initial temperature of each grid point for material 2(in Celsius)' (the second entry should be T2) and 'alpha2: the heat conductivity of material 2' (should be 'thermal diffusivity', as alpha2 is used interchangeably with alpha1 in dt = 1/(4*max(alpha1,alpha2))). Also steps 45.2/45.3 prompts contain a dangling cross-reference: 'the temperature array defined in .' (missing step number). All trivially inferable from the signature; unlikely to flip scores.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the duplicated 'T1' docstring entry to 'T2', change 'heat conductivity' to 'thermal diffusivity', and complete the dangling references to 'defined in step 45.1'.

overall_assessment: All four steps have well-formed, deterministic, non-degenerate targets and the full chain is reproducible bit-exactly with a natural numpy implementation (verified PASS on 45.1-45.4). However, the problem text actively misleads on two conventions that the targets then punish: (1) step 45.1's dimension-order sentence contradicts the actual (Nt, Ny, Nx) layout, and (2) step 45.3's explicit 'boundary normal should point outward' sentence is the OPPOSITE of the sign the targets encode on left/top boundaries, a defect that propagates into 45.4's scoring. Additionally, 45.4 silently requires BC enforcement on the initial slice. The problem is solvable, but a careful solver who follows the stated conventions literally is mis-scored on up to 3 of 4 steps; fixing the two convention sentences and adding one right/bottom Neumann test would make it fair.
